title: Native engine deadline test proves cancellation of a dispatched model call regardless of setup speed
user_story: As the owner I need the deadline-cancellation guarantee verified deterministically, not only when setup happens to finish within 20 ms.

requirements.description: The test dispatches the model call (asserted), then the task deadline cancels that same coroutine once, with no replay and no published report.

nonfunctional: Every original assertion kept; one assertion added
acceptance_criteria: Passes with a slow (50 ms) setup that made the old test fail exactly like Windows 3.12 CI

scenarios.expected: Started and cancelled exactly once; one model call; timeout kind
Policy refusal before dispatch still holds
A failed model call publishes nothing
Literature outage visible, not verified sources

recovery: Revert the test change. TASK-ENGINE-DEADLINE-661, max three cycles.
test_environment: RED and GREEN both ran with a temporary 50 ms sleep inserted in engine setup (emulating slow Windows CI) and removed immediately afterwards; product code is unchanged in the commit.

review.method: Same-agent review (not independent): deadline includes setup by design (phdlab.py remaining check); old 20 ms budget could expire before dispatch.

tdd.scope: RED: committed test with emulated 50 ms setup: 1/1 FAIL ([] != [True], identical to CI). GREEN: revised test with the same emulation: 1/1 PASS.
